agent_vs_you: The chain is right (exact script with write, then a synthetic female voice, then talking-photo of her own picture), and the words and identity came out right. The length was handled by hope. The plan had "Target delivery length: 8 seconds" in write and "pace delivery to exactly 8 seconds" in the voice extra, which voice.js passes to gpt-4o-mini-tts as a style instruction that it ignores. It also set seconds: 8 on voice, talking-photo and crop, and no code reads any of those. So the voice came out at 5.06 s, Magic Hour's talking photo took the audio's length (end_seconds = the sound's length, 5.12 s), and the crop kept 5.13 s. The agent had what it needed to see this coming: the planner prompt says "A voice track's length sets the clip length that carries it", and the write line gives 2.5 words a second, so 14 words is about 5.5 s and 8 s needs about 2.5 s of pauses that no listed tool adds. The final crop was also wasted: the portrait and the talking clip are already 640x640. I would build the 8 s into the voice track itself: one sentence per line, an unhurried delivery with a pause after each, and the track padded to exactly 8.0 s.

fix: Make voice.js honour params.seconds. After synthesis, if the speech is shorter than the target, spread the gap as pauses between lines (sentences) plus a short lead-in and tail (adelay/apad) until it is exactly the target. If it is longer, apply atempo up to 1.15 and report anything still over. Add to the catalogue's voice line: "its length sets talking-photo's length; seconds pads it with pauses". This applies to every timed voice-over and talking head, including E28b's 10 s narration.
evidence: ffprobe: speech.mp3 is 5.06 s; talking-portrait.mp4 is 640x640, 5.12 s, with audio; talking-portrait-square.mp4 is 720x720, 5.13 s. The grader frames show the curly-haired woman with changing mouth shapes. voice.js never reads params.seconds and sends extra as the TTS 'instructions'. execute.js builds talking-photo with end_seconds = the sound's length. The grader's 'about 8 s' window is 6.4 to 9.6 s, so 5.1 s fails correctly.
